recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34454 unless a future work group decision reintroduces XPath constraint generation or otherwise changes how datatype spreadsheet XPath columns are consumed.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive MnM issue reported that RatioRange inv-1 incorrectly rejected a RatioRange with highNumerator and denominator but no lowNumerator. The final resolution agreed to rewrite Ratio rat-1 and RatioRange inv-1 and to rename RatioRange inv-1/inv-2 to ratrng-1/ratrng-2 in R5, while noting the formula fixes were pre-applied in R4B.
initial_application: Commit 9c691ba64ee67ad143027cabf526318b5ae864f1 changed the Ratio and RatioRange datatype spreadsheet FHIRPath expressions from the xor forms to the clearer exists/empty forms. Commit 9b24283fc116fa7861fbd9b2d49c0c6b57ee800d later corrected the RatioRange TLA mapping to RatioRange=ratrng, enabling the R5 ratrng-prefixed generated constraint ids.
additional_context: Ratio and RatioRange are active datatypes in source/fhir.ini, and the R5 generated type snapshot in tools/history/release5/profiles-types.xml contains ratrng-1 and ratrng-2 with ratrng-1 carrying the corrected RatioRange FHIRPath expression. The RatioRange spreadsheet still has an old XPath-column value copied from Ratio, but ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath is disabled in the current datatype definition, so that value is not part of the current conformance surface.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Searches confirmed the corrected Ratio and RatioRange expressions are present, the old RatioRange xor expression is absent from the checked current source surfaces, and the R5 generated snapshot has ratrng-1/ratrng-2 keys.
